newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather forecasts sink home heating fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather forecasts sink home heating fuel prices.

text.p: Natural gas and heating oil prices fell Thursday at the New York Mercantile Exchange as traders expected a drop in home heating use when warm weather spreads throughout the central U.S. late this week.

Soybean prices moved lower in light holiday trading at the Chicago Board of Trade in reaction to ideal growing conditions for South America's young soybean crop. Hog futures rose ahead of Friday's Agriculture Department report, which should show a decline in hogs on U.S. farms.

Weather forecasters said 30- to 50-degree temperatures this weekend will replace the sub-zero temperatures and snow that blanketed the central U.S. since before Christmas. Minneapolis had its coldest Christmas on record when the mercury dipped to 27 below zero.
The latest National Weather Service forecast has above to much above normal temperatures spreading from California to the Appalacian Mountains.
"After today and tomorrow, it gets warmer. There's not much to hold it up," said one Texas-based producer of the natural gas price.
Natural gas prices declined despite expectations that the American Gas Association would report a decline in supplies in a report that was to be released after the market closed.
NYMEX natural gas for February delivery fell 0.321 cent to $3.384 per million Britsh thermal units.
"Heating oil pushed everything lower. If it weren't for heat, we may have gained today," said Dimon Oil trader Herbert Harris of prices in the crude oil complex.
"It was all due to the warmer forecasts," said an oil dealer, explaining heating oil's fall.

Heating oil for January delivery ended 1.34 cents a gallon lower at 70.06 cents on the New York Mercantile Exchange. January gasoline ended off 0.05 cent at 69.51 cents per gallon while February crude ended 18 cents lower at $24.92 a barrel.
CBOT soybean futures were pressured by reminders of the near-ideal soybean crop weather in Brazil and Argentina.
"There wasn't any other news," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. "It was pretty dull and it's likely to stay that way until at least the New Year."

The U.S. Agriculture Department estimates Brazil will harvest 26 million metric tons of soybeans early in 1997 versus 23.4 million a year ago, and Argentina should harvest 13 million tons versus 12.64 million a year ago.
CBOT soybeans for January delivery were down 5-1/4 cents at $7.01-3/4 per bushel and January soybean meal was off $2.00 at $230.90 per ton.
In hogs, expecations that Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report will be bullish to hog prices lifted nearby CME hog futures.

Analysts estimate the USDA report will show the U.S. hog herd, as of December 1, at 98.4 percent of a year ago. They also expect the report to show producers this year kept about two percent more female pigs for breeding rather than feeding them for slaughter.
CME February hog futures rose 0.65 cent to 76.750 cents per lb.
